title: nanomem 0.3.1 / engine 3.0.4 -- final honest scorecard against every competitor, on the standard retrieval task and the temporal supersession task
written_by: the scorecard agent; this file is assembled by a script that reads the results JSONs listed in `sources` and copies values out of them. No number here is hand-entered.

sources.standard_retrieval_before: the same path, as it stood before this session re-ran bench_competitors.py; its harness writes in place, so the pre-improvement values are embedded in this file under standard_retrieval.*.before
sources.temporal_before: the same path before this session re-ran bench_temporal.py; embedded here under temporal.arms.*.before
sources.temporal_extra_paired_tests: computed in this session by a script that re-uses bench_temporal.py's own dataset, pools, re-rankers and scorer; the per-question digits are embedded below so every interval can be recomputed from this file alone

dataset_meta.name: temporal-supersession benchmark

dataset_meta.note: Every proper noun is invented; see audit_vocabulary().

dataset.store_shape: one isolated store per synthetic user (personal-memory deployment shape); every arm gets the identical shape

No 'before' number exists and none can be produced: the pre-improvement tree is not in git (HEAD 441aaca already contains the new entities.py), and scoring a second build would burn the set.

second_arm_declared_in_advance.why: benchmark_clean_chat_v3r2.py passes temporal_direction on every query; chat.py and cli.py never do. Both arms were declared before either was scored and both are reported.

strictness_matched_control.why: persona4 has 0 of 36 queries whose expected substring occurs in more than one stored turn; clean_chat_benchmark.json has 10 of 36 and the held-out set 4 of 24 (clean_chat_benchmark_persona4.json -> difficulty_comparability.scoring_strictness). The older sets are therefore scored more leniently than persona4 BY CONSTRUCTION. Here they are re-scored under persona4's own rule. persona4 is not re-scored and no persona4 question was inspected.

memory_context.note: the competitor harness measures the LOADER shape (one process ingests 71,433 documents and then serves). bench_memory.py separates it from the SERVER shape (open a vault another process wrote, then serve). The server figure has no competitor counterpart in this work -- bench_competitors.py does not measure one -- so it is context, not a head-to-head.

gate_definition.reproducible: routed p50 < exhaustive p50 in EVERY replicate

recall.result: SIX-WAY TIE AT THE EXACT CEILING
recall.reading: exactness is a CEILING, not an edge. nanomem does not beat any exact engine on recall and cannot; what it does is sit in the tied group while Chroma's default configuration does not.

temporal_supersession.result: nanomem WINS this axis on the improved build, having lost it on the build measured before this session. The margin over the strongest competitor arm is small (+4.3 pts) and survives a user-level cluster bootstrap; the margin over the two-way recency heuristic is large (+17.8 pts).

adjacent_attribute.reading: still NET NEGATIVE against doing nothing: the layer merges sibling attributes that plain cosine keeps apart

third_party.reading: still NET NEGATIVE against doing nothing, and against the competitor heuristic, which is at 100.0

documented_metadata_entity_path.reading: REGRESSION. Using the DOCUMENTED metadata['entity'] tag now scores far BELOW the shipped default and below the same-gift competitor oracle. It also fell against the pre-improvement build.

passing_temporal_direction.reading: passing the two-way temporal_direction argument now COSTS 13.2 pts, because it overrides the engine's own three-way reading of the question. The documented argument is now a footgun.

paired.note: previous_value (56 of 326 questions) is excluded: it is the type both oracles score 0.0 on. These are the three types both systems claim to handle.

excluding_previous_value.reading: on the three question types both systems claim to handle, nanomem's +4.4 over the heuristic is barely significant and it LOSES to the oracle competitor by 10.7 pts

personal_memory_chat.result: THE TARGET IS MISSED. The clean estimate is 63.9%, against a >=80% target -- 16.1 points short. The burned set did NOT improve: 75.0% -> 70.8% (18/24 -> 17/24), a one-question regression on n=24. Under persona4's own strict scoring rule the burned set reads 65.0% and persona4 63.9%, so most of the 75.0 -> 63.9 gap is SCORING LENIENCY in the older fixture, not contamination -- and the honest clean level for this task is about 64%, not 75%.

verdict.one_sentence_positioning: nanomem 0.3.1 is an exact vector store that ties FAISS, sqlite-vec and a tuned Chroma at the recall ceiling (60.6% evidence recall@4 at 71,433 docs) while being 1.66x slower than FAISS, 3.6x heavier in peak RSS and the smallest on disk of the stores that keep the text -- and its one real differentiator, entity-aware temporal supersession, now beats a test-set-tuned recency heuristic on Chroma by +4.3 pts [+0.9, +7.7] at shipped defaults with zero configuration, but is still worse than plain cosine on sibling attributes and third-party facts and still scores only 63.9% on a never-before-scored chat set against an 80% target.

known_gaps: SINGLE RUN PER (arm, corpus). One insertion order (rng(0)), one embedding model (nomic-embed-text 768-d), one machine. There are no confidence intervals on latency, ingest, disk or RSS anywhere in this scorecard -- only on recall (paired bootstrap, 10,000 resamples) and on the temporal top-1 deltas.

THE BEFORE COLUMN IS NOT A CLEAN A/B. bench_competitors.py and bench_temporal.py write their results in place, so the pre-improvement values embedded here were produced by a run 3 hours earlier on a machine under different load (competitor before-run load average is in that block). Recall and top-1 are deterministic and reproduce exactly; the latency and RSS 'before' figures should be read as a different run, not a controlled baseline.

NO BEFORE NUMBER EXISTS FOR persona4. The pre-improvement tree is not recoverable from git (HEAD 441aaca already contains the new entities.py), and scoring a second build would burn the set. So the 63.9% is an absolute level, not a delta: this scorecard cannot say whether the ranking work helped or hurt on a clean chat set. What it can say is that on the BURNED chat set the same work moved 75.0% -> 70.8%.
n=24 AND n=36 ON THE CHAT SETS. The 75.0 -> 70.8 change on the held-out set is ONE question. No significance is claimed for it in either direction, and none should be read into it.

THE TEMPORAL SET IS 10 SYNTHETIC USERS, ~46 documents each. The question-level bootstrap is optimistic because questions within a user are not independent; a user-level cluster bootstrap is reported alongside every headline pair and the +4.3 pt win survives it (CI [+1.5, +7.4]). Cross-user leakage in a shared multi-tenant vault is not measured, and nothing here says how the cosine-window grouping behaves at 10k+ rows per user.

THE COMPETITOR'S TEMPORAL PARAMETERS WERE SWEPT ON THE TEST SET and kept at the competitor's optimum (kpool=3, delta=0.08). That gift is deliberate and stays. nanomem got no tuning of any kind on that set. The dev-tuned competitor variants and the 8-user holdout are reported and give the same ordering.

THE THREE-WAY COMPETITOR ARM IS NOT A LIBRARY FEATURE EITHER. chroma_recency_3way needs a hand-written three-way direction classifier on top of Chroma; nanomem_default needs nothing. That asymmetry favours nanomem in deployment terms and is not captured by the top-1 number.

THE STANDARD BENCHMARK DOES NOT EXERCISE THE TEMPORAL LAYER AT ALL. The corpus is HotpotQA paragraphs stored with source='wiki', which is not in nanomem.entities.PERSONAL_SOURCES, so the layer is inert by design -- proven empirically by the engine matching FAISS on 499 of 500 queries. The two tasks in this scorecard measure two disjoint code paths.

PEAK RSS IS THE LOADER SHAPE. The competitor harness ingests and serves in one process, so nanomem's 826.4 MB includes the ingest high-water mark. bench_memory.py measures a SERVER shape of 286.0 MB for the same corpus, but bench_competitors.py measures no server-shape figure for FAISS, Chroma or sqlite-vec, so there is no like-for-like server comparison in this work. Do not pair the 286.0 MB with the competitors' numbers.

FAISS's 209.3 MiB INDEX STORES NO TEXT. nanomem's 148.7 MiB contains the corpus text as well, so the disk axis is only like-for-like against sqlite-vec and Chroma. No engine was VACUUMed or force-compacted.
recall@4 IS THE FIRST FOUR OF A k=10 QUERY, which is identical to k=4 for the exact arms and a small gift to the HNSW arms. Chroma's deficits are if anything understated.
NO THREAD PINNING. FAISS had 12 OMP threads, Chroma built on ~4.5 cores, nanomem used numpy/Accelerate defaults. The latency column is an out-of-the-box comparison, not a single-core one.

THE findings BLOCK INSIDE temporal_bench_results.json NOW CONTRADICTS ITS OWN NUMBERS. Its `claim` strings were written for the pre-improvement build and are not regenerated ('shipped_default_has_no_net_benefit' now carries 90.5 against a floor of 47.9). That file is not owned by this agent. Read its numbers, not its prose.

THE ROUTER ARM IN THE STANDARD TABLE IS NOT A SHIPPED CONFIGURATION: n_exhaustive was lowered from 50,000 to 1,000 so routing engages at every size. At shipped defaults it is byte-identical to the exact arm below 50k documents.
NOTHING HERE MEASURES END-TO-END ANSWER QUALITY WITH AN LLM IN THE LOOP, encryption on, multi-tenant filtering at scale, or any corpus that is not HotpotQA or a synthetic personal log.

They ran from a session-local scratchpad that does not survive, so their source is embedded here and the measurements can be reproduced from this file alone.
scripts_embedded.temporal_extra_pairs.py:
"""Extra PAIRED head-to-heads on the temporal-supersession set.

bench_temporal.py computes a fixed HEADLINES list of paired bootstraps and drops
its per-question vectors before writing its JSON.  After the ranking-layer work
the arm that matters is `nanomem_default` (shipped defaults, no argument passed)
and the comparison that matters is against the STRONGEST competitor arm
(chroma_recency_3way, swept on the test set in the competitor's favour).  That
pair is not in HEADLINES, so it is computed here, re-using bench_temporal's own
dataset, embeddings, pools, re-rankers and scorer so the numbers are the same
numbers.  Per-question correctness digits are written out so the intervals can
be recomputed from this file alone.
"""
import json, os, sys
import numpy as np

HERE = "<repo>/corpora/refound"
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
import bench_temporal as bt   # noqa: E402

OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/tmp/temporal_extra_pairs.json"

dataset = json.load(open(bt.DATASET_PATH))
table = bt.embed_all(dataset)
all_questions, docindex, packs = [], {}, []
for u in dataset["users"]:
    for d in u["docs"]:
        docindex[d["id"]] = d
    all_questions += u["questions"]
    packs.append(dict(
        user_id=u["user_id"], docs=u["docs"], questions=u["questions"],
        ids=[d["id"] for d in u["docs"]],
        ts=np.array([d["ts"] for d in u["docs"]], dtype=np.float64),
        V=np.stack([table[d["text"]] for d in u["docs"]]).astype(np.float32),
        qvec={q["qid"]: table[q["text"]].astype(np.float32) for q in u["questions"]},
        table=table))

key_of = lambda did: (docindex[did]["subject"], docindex[did]["attribute"])
dir_current = lambda q: "current"
dir_wording = lambda q: bt.wording_direction(q["text"])
dir_wording3 = lambda q: bt.wording_direction_3way(q["text"])

pools = {"exact": {}, "chroma": {}}
for pk in packs:
    pools["exact"].update(bt.pools_exact(pk))
    pools["chroma"].update(bt.pools_chroma(pk))

res = json.load(open(bt.RESULTS_PATH))
kp = res["sweeps"]["chroma_recency"]["chosen"]["kpool"]
dl = res["sweeps"]["chroma_recency"]["chosen"]["delta"]
print("[cfg] chroma_recency swept optimum kpool=%d delta=%.3f" % (kp, dl))

ranked = {}
ranked["exact_cosine_floor"] = {q["qid"]: [c[0] for c in pools["exact"][q["qid"]][:5]]
                                for q in all_questions}
ranked["chroma_recency"] = bt.rerank_arm(pools["chroma"], all_questions, dir_wording, dl, kp)
ranked["chroma_recency_3way"] = bt.rerank_arm(pools["chroma"], all_questions, dir_wording3, dl, kp)
ranked["chroma_oracle_group"] = bt.rerank_arm(
    pools["chroma"], all_questions, dir_wording, 0.0, bt.POOL_MAX,
    oracle="doc", key_of=key_of)

for arm, dfn, kw in (("nanomem_default", dir_current, {}),
                     ("nanomem_wording_dir_3way", dir_wording3, {"three_way": True})):
    out = {}
    for pk in packs:
        r, _ = bt.run_nanomem(pk, dfn, arm, **kw)
        out.update(r)
    ranked[arm] = out

test_qs = [q for q in all_questions if q["qid"][:3] not in bt.DEV_USERS]


def vec(name, qs):
    rk = ranked[name]
    return np.array([1.0 if rk.get(q["qid"], [None])[:1] == [q["gold_id"]] else 0.0
                     for q in qs])


def paired(a, b, qs, iters=10000, seed=7):
    va, vb = vec(a, qs), vec(b, qs)
    d = va - vb
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    idx = rng.integers(0, len(d), size=(iters, len(d)))
    boots = d[idx].mean(axis=1) * 100.0
    lo, hi = np.percentile(boots, [2.5, 97.5])
    return dict(a=a, b=b, n=len(qs),
                a_top1_pct=round(float(va.mean() * 100), 1),
                b_top1_pct=round(float(vb.mean() * 100), 1),
                delta_pts=round(float(d.mean() * 100), 1),
                ci95=[round(float(lo), 1), round(float(hi), 1)],
                significant=bool(lo > 0 or hi < 0))


def cluster_paired(a, b, qs, iters=10000, seed=13):
    """USER-level cluster bootstrap: resample the 10 users, not the questions.

    bench_temporal's own note says the question-level interval is optimistic
    because questions inside one user are not independent.  This is the wider,
    honest version."""
    users = sorted({q["qid"][:3] for q in qs})
    byu = {u: [q for q in qs if q["qid"][:3] == u] for u in users}
    dv = {u: float((vec(a, byu[u]) - vec(b, byu[u])).mean() * 100) for u in users}
    n_q = {u: len(byu[u]) for u in users}
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    boots = []
    for _ in range(iters):
        pick = rng.integers(0, len(users), size=len(users))
        num = sum(dv[users[i]] * n_q[users[i]] for i in pick)
        den = sum(n_q[users[i]] for i in pick)
        boots.append(num / den)
    lo, hi = np.percentile(boots, [2.5, 97.5])
    va, vb = vec(a, qs), vec(b, qs)
    return dict(a=a, b=b, n_users=len(users), n_questions=len(qs),
                a_top1_pct=round(float(va.mean() * 100), 1),
                b_top1_pct=round(float(vb.mean() * 100), 1),
                delta_pts=round(float((va - vb).mean() * 100), 1),
                ci95=[round(float(lo), 1), round(float(hi), 1)],
                significant=bool(lo > 0 or hi < 0))


PAIRS = [("nanomem_default", "exact_cosine_floor"),
         ("nanomem_default", "chroma_recency"),
         ("nanomem_default", "chroma_recency_3way"),
         ("nanomem_default", "chroma_oracle_group"),
         ("nanomem_wording_dir_3way", "chroma_recency_3way")]

out = dict(
    what="paired head-to-heads that bench_temporal.py's fixed HEADLINES list "
         "does not compute, against the improved build",
    script=os.path.abspath(__file__),
    source_of_competitor_config=dict(file=os.path.basename(bt.RESULTS_PATH),
                                     kpool=kp, delta=dl,
                                     note="swept on the TEST set in the "
                                          "competitor's favour, as bench_temporal does"),
    top1_pct={k: round(float(vec(k, all_questions).mean() * 100), 1) for k in ranked},
    top1_pct_test_users_only={k: round(float(vec(k, test_qs).mean() * 100), 1) for k in ranked},
    question_level_bootstrap_all=[paired(a, b, all_questions) for a, b in PAIRS],
    question_level_bootstrap_test_users=[paired(a, b, test_qs) for a, b in PAIRS],
    user_level_cluster_bootstrap_all=[cluster_paired(a, b, all_questions) for a, b in PAIRS],
    per_question=dict(
        note="one digit per question, same order as qids, 1 = gold id ranked "
             "first. Recompute any interval in this file from these.",
        qids=[q["qid"] for q in all_questions],
        arms={k: "".join(str(int(x)) for x in vec(k, all_questions)) for k in ranked}),
)
json.dump(out, open(OUT, "w"), indent=1)
print("\n[out] %s" % OUT)
for row in out["question_level_bootstrap_all"]:
    print("  %-26s - %-22s %+6.1f pts CI [%+.1f,%+.1f] %s"
          % (row["a"], row["b"], row["delta_pts"], row["ci95"][0], row["ci95"][1],
             "" if row["significant"] else "(ns)"))
print("[user-level cluster bootstrap]")
for row in out["user_level_cluster_bootstrap_all"]:
    print("  %-26s - %-22s %+6.1f pts CI [%+.1f,%+.1f] %s"
          % (row["a"], row["b"], row["delta_pts"], row["ci95"][0], row["ci95"][1],
             "" if row["significant"] else "(ns)"))
scripts_embedded.chat_nodir_arm.py:
"""The SECOND, pre-declared arm on a clean_chat fixture: no temporal_direction.

benchmark_clean_chat_v3r2.py -- the script that produced the 75.0% held-out
figure -- passes `temporal_direction=q["temporal_direction"]` on every query.
chat.py and cli.py never pass it.  On the temporal-supersession set the improved
build scores 90.5% with no argument and 77.3% when the two-way argument is
passed, so which arm you run is not a detail.  BOTH arms were declared before
either was scored; neither is selected after the fact.

Everything else -- fixture, gold-store rule, reopen, top-1 substring test -- is
copied from benchmark_clean_chat_v3r2.py unchanged.
"""
import json, os, sys, tempfile

HERE = "<repo>/corpora/refound"
PKG = "<repo>/nanomem_standalone"
sys.path.insert(0, PKG)
from nanomem.vault import Vault   # noqa: E402

fixture = sys.argv[1]
B = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, fixture)))
out = {"fixture": fixture, "arm": "no temporal_direction argument (chat.py path)",
       "personas": [s["persona"] for s in B["sets"]], "arms": {}}

for pass_dir in (False, True):
    gold = {"top1": 0, "top3": 0, "n": 0}
    per = {}
    for s in B["sets"]:
        turns, queries = s["turns"], s["verification_queries"]
        idx = {t["original_index"]: t for t in turns}
        d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        path = os.path.join(d, "v.dat")
        v = Vault(path)
        for t in turns:
            if t["should_store"]:
                v.add(t["text"], source="chat_session",
                      metadata={"user_id": s["persona"]})
        v.flush(); v.close()
        v = Vault(path)
        h1 = n = 0
        for q in queries:
            src = idx.get(q["source_turn_index"])
            if src is None or not src["should_store"]:
                continue
            kw = {"temporal_direction": q["temporal_direction"]} if pass_dir else {}
            hits = v.search(q["query"], top_k=3, **kw)
            texts = [h["text"] for h in hits]
            gold["n"] += 1; n += 1
            ok = bool(texts) and q["expected_substring"] in texts[0]
            gold["top1"] += ok; h1 += ok
            gold["top3"] += any(q["expected_substring"] in t for t in texts)
        per[s["persona"]] = {"top1": h1, "n": n}
        v.close()
    name = "explicit_direction" if pass_dir else "no_direction_argument"
    out["arms"][name] = dict(
        gold_stores={**gold,
                     "top1_pct": round(100 * gold["top1"] / max(gold["n"], 1), 1),
                     "top3_pct": round(100 * gold["top3"] / max(gold["n"], 1), 1)},
        gold_per_persona=per)
    print("[%s / %s] gold-store top1 %s%% top3 %s%% (n=%d)"
          % (fixture, name, out["arms"][name]["gold_stores"]["top1_pct"],
             out["arms"][name]["gold_stores"]["top3_pct"], gold["n"]))
print(json.dumps(out["arms"]))
json.dump(out, open(sys.argv[2], "w"), indent=1)
scripts_embedded.chat_strictness_matched.py:
"""Strictness-matched chat scoring.

persona4 is documented (clean_chat_benchmark_persona4.json ->
difficulty_comparability.scoring_strictness) as having ZERO queries whose
expected substring appears in more than one stored turn, while
clean_chat_benchmark.json has 10 of 36 and the burned held-out set 4 of 24.  A
non-unique substring can credit a top-1 hit that landed on the wrong turn, so
the older sets are scored more leniently than persona4 by construction.

This re-scores the OLDER sets restricted to their unique-substring queries only,
so they are judged by persona4's rule.  persona4 itself is NOT touched here --
every one of its queries already satisfies the rule, so its 63.9% is already the
strict number, and nothing about which persona4 questions failed is inspected.
"""
import json, os, sys, tempfile

HERE = "<repo>/corpora/refound"
sys.path.insert(0, "<repo>/nanomem_standalone")
from nanomem.vault import Vault   # noqa: E402

out = {"rule": "keep only queries whose expected_substring occurs in exactly one "
               "STORED turn of that persona -- persona4's own rule, applied to "
               "the older sets",
       "fixtures": {}}
for fixture in sys.argv[1:-1]:
    B = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, fixture)))
    kept = dropped = 0
    gold = {"top1": 0, "top3": 0, "n": 0}
    for s in B["sets"]:
        turns, queries = s["turns"], s["verification_queries"]
        idx = {t["original_index"]: t for t in turns}
        stored = [t["text"] for t in turns if t["should_store"]]
        d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        path = os.path.join(d, "v.dat")
        v = Vault(path)
        for t in turns:
            if t["should_store"]:
                v.add(t["text"], source="chat_session",
                      metadata={"user_id": s["persona"]})
        v.flush(); v.close()
        v = Vault(path)
        for q in queries:
            src = idx.get(q["source_turn_index"])
            if src is None or not src["should_store"]:
                continue
            occ = sum(1 for t in stored if q["expected_substring"] in t)

                            temporal_direction=q["temporal_direction"])

            gold["n"] += 1
            gold["top1"] += bool(texts) and q["expected_substring"] in texts[0]
            gold["top3"] += any(q["expected_substring"] in t for t in texts)
        v.close()
    out["fixtures"][fixture] = dict(
        kept=kept, dropped=dropped, **gold,
        top1_pct=round(100 * gold["top1"] / max(gold["n"], 1), 1),
        top3_pct=round(100 * gold["top3"] / max(gold["n"], 1), 1))
    print("[%s] unique-substring queries only: %d kept, %d dropped -> top1 %d/%d = %.1f%%"
          % (fixture, kept, dropped, gold["top1"], gold["n"],
             out["fixtures"][fixture]["top1_pct"]))
